newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices retreat, await data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - Prices retreat, await data.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices retreated to around unchanged to down one-eighth of a point, losing some of the strength they displayed earlier as short-covering abated in U.S. Treasuries.

Traders said players now appeared to have squared positions in U.S. government securities ahead of Friday morning's release of the September employment data, which is expected to show only moderate growth.
A consensus survey of economists polled by Reuters found that they look for jobs to have risen by 166,000.
The payrolls data has prompted sharp responses from the market this year, which at times seems to have gone into the data in an over-sold position. That might not be the case this Friday.
"If anything, I'd say there's more complacency in the market going into the number tomorrow," a trader said.

In the municipal market, both the primary and secondary markets were active, with traders saying that as has been typical this year, once institutions buy new issues, they tend to turn around and sell off some of their inventories.
The bid-wanted lists that were circulated included a fairly wide range of types of issues, as institutions sought to improve the structure of their holdings.
"Accounts, as they have been for really the whole year, if they buy some of the new deals, they tend to post their worst-structured bonds," a trader said.
As examples, he cited issues with shorter calls, bonds with maturities of 15 to 20 years, original issue discount bonds, and a few high-yield bonds.

December municipal bond futures traded on the Chicago Board of Trade shed three ticks to 115-2/32, while December Treasury bond futures eased two ticks to 110-8/32. This left the MOB spread between the two futures at plus 154 ticks, little changed from levels seen this week.
In the primary market, sizable offerings included the District of Colombia's $168.9 million of general obligation bonds, which Merrill Lynch said it won at a true interest cost of 6.534 percent.

In the secondary market, actively quoted issues included Metropolitan Pier and Exposition Authority Illinios Dedicated State Tax Revenue Refunding of June 2027. The bonds, which have a 5-1/4 percent coupon, were bid at 5.81 percent NET, up two basis points from levels seen on Wednesday.
And Cook County Illinois Capital Improvement Original Issue Discount of November 2022, which have a 5-7/8 percent coupon, were bid at 99-3/4, unchanged from Wednesday.
